get.description:
The metric alarms you can see in this org, with current state and channels.

Filtered per alarm, not per request: org-level alarms (credits, org-wide spend) need `alarms.read`, and an alarm tagged to a project needs `projects.alarms.read` on that project. Holding one and not the other returns the matching subset rather than a `403`, so a role scoped to a single project sees exactly that project's alarms.

post.description:
Create a metric alarm with a threshold over evaluation periods.

Set `denominator_metric_name` for a **rate** rather than a count: the datapoint becomes `metric_name / denominator_metric_name` and `threshold` reads as a fraction (`0.05` = 5%). Prefer this for anything that scales with traffic — a fixed error count pages at 3am once the org grows. Pair it with `min_sample_count` so a single failure in a quiet minute isn't a 100% error rate.

Both series must be binned on the same clock, since they are divided period by period. For outcome rates that means `app.run.terminal_count` — runs that *finished* in the period — and not `app.run.count`, which counts runs that *started* and includes ones still running. Mismatched pairs are rejected.

Ratio alarms also require `stat` `sum` or `count`. The stat is applied to each series and the two results divided, so only stats that add up across the minutes in a period come out as a rate — `avg` would divide two means and `min`/`max` would take their extremes from different minutes. Other stats are rejected rather than silently producing a number that isn't a rate.

A sustained incident only ever notifies once, so repeat messages mean the alarm is flapping. Three levers fix that, and which one depends on the metric: `clear_threshold` (fire high, clear low) for continuous series like rates and latencies; `datapoints_to_alarm` for spiky ones that cross the line briefly; and `missing_data: "ignore"` for sparse ones, where a minute with no traffic is absence of evidence rather than a recovery.

Set `group_by` to watch every app, project or label separately with one alarm: `workforce_id` keeps one state per app, `project_id` one per project, `label` one per label (the model, for `llm.cache.*`). Without it the alarm reads the sum of whatever `dims` leaves out, where a small app that is entirely broken disappears behind a large healthy one. Each evaluation sends one message listing the groups that entered alarm and the ones that recovered; the alarm's own `state` is `alarm` while any group is, and `groups` on the alarm lists each one. An app created later is covered from its first datapoint. `missing_data` defaults to `ignore` here, so an app that goes quiet overnight keeps its state; one that stays quiet for 72 hours is dropped, with a message if it was in alarm. `group_by` can't be changed after creation, can't be combined with a percentile `stat` or the credit and budget levels, and the dimension it names must be left out of `dims`.

Use `GET /orgs/{org_id}/metrics/catalog` to see which metric names and labels this org is actually emitting. Two metrics won't be listed until you alarm on them: `org.credits.usage_pct` (percent of the billing period's prepaid budget consumed) and `org.credits.remaining` (credits left in it) are only sampled for orgs that have an enabled alarm on one, since the underlying read is the billing gate's and too heavy to run speculatively. Both are levels sampled once a minute, so use `max`, `avg` or `min` — `sum` would add one reading per minute in the period and is rejected. `org.credits.remaining` goes negative under overage.

Percent and headroom are worth having separately: 95% of a large budget can still be thousands of credits, while 50% of a small one is one bad afternoon. For burn *volume* rather than budget position, alarm on `org.credits.spend` with `sum` — that one carries `project_id` and `workforce_id` dims, so it can scope to a single project or workforce the way the org's budget can't.

Credit budgets (`GET …/billing/budgets`) have the same two levels, one series per budget: `budget.usage_pct` (percent of its limit used this period) and `budget.remaining` (credits left; for a `project_reserve`, what it still holds). Name the budget with `dims.label` — its type and target: `project:42`, `project_reserve:42`, `role:7`, `user:299` or `user_default` — which survives saves, unlike the budget id. An alarm without a budget label is rejected. For `role` and `user_default`, which cap each user separately, the series is the top spender's, the first the gate would block. Any threshold works, and several alarms on one budget (50, 80 and 100) are the way to get stepped warnings. Like the org's levels they are sampled once a minute only for orgs alarming on them, reject `sum`, and need `billing.read` as well as the alarm permission.

For latency, `stat` accepts any percentile from `p0.1` to `p99.9`, in tenths. Equivalent spellings are fine (`p95.0` is accepted and comes back as `p95`), but anything finer than a tenth is rejected rather than rounded, so an alarm never silently watches a different point than the one you asked for. These are exact, computed over the individual run durations rather than interpolated from bins, which is also why they are limited to `app.run.duration_ms`, cannot be a ratio, and cannot carry `label`, `project_env_id` or `dims.deployment_id` — a run row has no such column, so those filters would silently widen the alarm to everything. Prefer a high percentile over `avg` for latency: an average hides the tail that users actually notice, and hides it harder as traffic grows.

Two different project fields, gated separately. Top-level `project_id` is ownership — who may see and edit the alarm afterwards — and setting it requires `projects.alarms.manage` on that project, while leaving it out makes an org-level alarm and requires `alarms.manage`. `dims.project_id` only narrows which metric bins are read, but it still exposes that project's numbers through the alarm's notifications, so it requires `projects.alarms.read` on the project it names.

get.summary: Find alarms that stopped receiving data
get.description:
For every enabled alarm, when the metric series behind it last produced a datapoint.

Answers the one question an alarm's own `state` cannot: is it still watching anything? Under the default `not_breaching` policy an alarm whose metric stopped being emitted — a deleted workforce, a disabled trace filter, a renamed metric — sits at `ok` indefinitely and looks identical to one that is genuinely healthy.

`stale` marks silence lasting ten evaluation windows (minimum one hour), which is long enough that a quiet-but-live series won't trip it. A brand-new alarm reads as stale until its first datapoint, which is accurate: it cannot fire yet.

For a ratio alarm, `last_datapoint_at` is the **older** of the two series, since a period only yields a datapoint where both sides have one. A live numerator over a dead denominator is therefore reported as stale — every period resolves to a missing ratio, so the alarm is blind despite one of its series still flowing. `denominator_last_datapoint_at` tells you which side went quiet.

Covers the same alarms `GET /orgs/{org_id}/alarms` returns for you, so `healthy` and `stale_count` describe your visible subset — a project-scoped caller gets their project's blind spots, not the org's.

Needs `alarms.read` for an org-level alarm, or `projects.alarms.read` on the owning project for a project alarm.

patch.description:
Update alarm thresholds, evaluation settings, or enabled state.

`clear_threshold` is the one field where `null` differs from omitting the key: send `null` to drop the hysteresis, omit it to leave it as is. It is validated against the resulting `threshold` and `comparison`, so patching either side of the pair alone can't invert them.

`metric_name` and `denominator_metric_name` are not patchable: changing what an alarm watches would leave its state and history describing a different question, so define a new alarm instead.

`enabled: true` requires at least one attached channel. Channels may be detached freely while an alarm is disabled, so this is what stops that from re-enabling an alarm that evaluates and records transitions with nowhere to notify.

The alarm's owning project is not patchable either, so the permission needed here is fixed for the life of the alarm: `alarms.manage` when it is org-level, `projects.alarms.manage` on the owner when it is not.

schema.description: Successful responses use HTTP 204 and do not include a body.

post.summary: Attach a channel to an alarm
post.description:
Attach another notification channel to an alarm, so one condition reaches several destinations (page Slack and email the on-call, say).

Accepts the same channel shape as alarm creation: `{ "id": <channel id> }` to reuse an existing channel, or inline `type` + `config` to create one. Inline channels identical to an existing row are deduped rather than duplicated.

Idempotent — re-attaching a channel that is already linked returns `already_linked: true` and changes nothing.

Gated by the alarm, not the channel: `alarms.manage` for an org-level alarm, `projects.alarms.manage` on the owner for a project alarm. Channels themselves are org-wide, so a project-scoped caller can point their alarm at any existing channel — attaching one is a routing decision about their alarm, whereas creating or deleting the channel row needs `notification_channels.manage`.

delete.summary: Detach a channel from an alarm
delete.description:
Detach a channel from an alarm. The `NotificationChannels` row itself is left alone — other alarms and notification rules may still be using it.

Removing the **last** channel from an enabled alarm is rejected: it would keep evaluating and recording transitions while notifying nobody, which looks healthy from the outside. To swap a sole channel, attach the replacement first; to silence an alarm, `PATCH` it with `enabled: false`.

schema.description: Successful responses use HTTP 204 and do not include a body.

Metric names and label values actually recorded for this org in the recent past. Use it to populate a metric picker: `GET /orgs/{org_id}/metrics` requires a name, and alarms reference names that only exist once something has emitted them.

`origin` separates the two kinds: `system` metrics (`app.*`, `deployment.*`, `org.*`) are emitted by the platform and have no configuration, while `custom` ones come from a metric definition — see `definition_ids` for the config behind them.

This reports what is *flowing*, not what is configured, so the two can disagree in both directions: a definition that has never matched a span will not appear, and a deleted definition's series stays until its bins age out.

Needs `analytics.read` for the org-wide catalog. Passing `project_id` narrows it to series carrying that project's dimension and accepts `projects.alarms.read` there instead, so a project-scoped role gets a working metric picker. That view omits series with no project dimension, `org.credits.*` among them — which are org-level metrics that caller cannot alarm on anyway.

permission needed from `analytics.read` to `projects.alarms.read` on
this project.

get.description:
The org's custom metric definitions and their current predicates.

`project_id` filters to what is *in effect* for that project, which includes org-wide definitions (those with no `project_id`) since they run against that project's runs too.

This lists configuration, not data. A definition that has never matched a span appears here but not in `GET /orgs/{org_id}/metrics/catalog`.

Filtered per definition the same way `GET /orgs/{org_id}/alarms` is: org-wide definitions need `alarms.read`, project ones need `projects.alarms.read` on the owner. So a project-scoped caller sees their own definitions but not the org-wide ones that also run against their runs, even with `project_id` set.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description:

in the org.

post.description:
Define a metric of your own, emitted as runs land. Once it exists it behaves like any platform metric: readable through `GET /orgs/{org_id}/metrics`, listed in the catalog with `origin: custom`, and alarmable with no extra setup.

The definition is a span predicate over each completed run's trace. Span paths are `{workforce}.{step}` and matching is on the **leaf**: use `llm` or `get_address`, not the full path. Predicate fields AND together and all are optional — omitting every one matches every non-root span.

`metric_name` is forced under the reserved `trace.` prefix so a definition cannot shadow a platform series. Set `label_source` to `span_name` to break the metric out per step, then point an alarm at a single step with `dims.label`.

Definitions are **not retroactive**: matching happens as runs arrive, so a new definition only sees traces written after it. Dry-run it against stored traces first with `POST /orgs/{org_id}/metrics/definitions/preview`. Note also that only sum/count/avg/min/max are available on the result — percentiles are not derivable from metric bins.

Set `project_id` to scope the definition to one project, which also makes it editable by holders of `projects.alarms.manage` there. Leaving it out defines an org-wide metric that runs against every project's traces, and needs `alarms.manage`.

Run a candidate predicate against recent stored traces without saving it, and see what it would have recorded.

Definitions are not retroactive, so a saved predicate that matches nothing looks identical to one that matches nothing *yet*. This answers that before you commit: which spans matched, what values they'd contribute, and how many distinct labels the metric would carry.

Samples the newest runs (20 by default, 50 max) — enough to tell a working predicate from a broken one, not a measurement of the true rate. Pass `workforce_id` to make the sample representative of the agent you're actually matching. This is the only endpoint that reads stored traces, which is why it is capped; do not poll it.

Because it returns trace content, `project_id` doubles as the permission target: omit it and the sample spans the whole org, which needs `alarms.manage`; set it and the sample is capped to that project, which needs `projects.alarms.manage` there. A caller scoped to one project must therefore pass it.

delete.description:
Stop emitting a custom metric. Takes effect within one flush interval (~10s).

Bins the definition already wrote are kept — they are real observations — and age out with normal metric retention, so the series stays readable and keeps appearing in the catalog for a while with no definition behind it. Alarms pointing at the metric are left alone and will fall to `insufficient_data` once the series stops.

Needs `alarms.manage` for an org-wide definition, or `projects.alarms.manage` on the owning project for a project one.

schema.description: Successful responses use HTTP 204 and do not include a body.

patch.summary: Rename or enable/disable a custom metric definition
patch.description:
Only the name and the enabled flag are mutable. The predicate and destination metric are fixed at creation: changing them would splice two different meanings into one series with nothing marking the seam, so a changed definition should be a new definition.

Disabling stops new observations within one flush interval (~10s). Bins already written stay and age out with normal metric retention.

The owning project is not mutable either, so the permission needed here is fixed: `alarms.manage` for an org-wide definition, `projects.alarms.manage` on the owner for a project one.

deployment the organization is routed to doesn't serve the model.
`policy`: an admin's rule.

active_version.description: Spec version the proxy routes with; absent until one is activated.

shadow_version.description:
Version evaluated alongside the active one on every decision (same
features and answers, never served): what it would change shows in
stats before activating it.

slug.description:

app links.

AceBaseStatus.description: The active version against today's platform default.

compiles.description:
Whether it still composes with today's default. `false` = the proxy
serves the platform default for it (`invalid_spec` fallback) until a
fixed version is activated; `errors` say why.

saved_against.description: The one the version was checked against when saved.

AceCacheStat.description:
Prompt cache use of the calls one model served for one app. Token counts
are the billed usage of the calls whose prompt was large enough to be
cached (`ACE_CACHEABLE_PROMPT_TOKENS`); smaller ones are only counted.

app_id.description: Null = calls made without an app.

calls.description: Calls large enough to be cached.

hit_rate.description:
`cache_read_tokens / input_tokens`. Anthropic's reference for agent
loops is a median of 0.84; below about 0.8 something is usually
breaking the cache.

input_tokens.description: Their prompt tokens: read from cache, written to it, or neither.

small_calls.description: Calls too small to be cached, left out of everything above.

uncached_calls.description:
Claude calls that neither read nor wrote the cache: served by the
OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which does not cache.

expect.description:
Any of `route`, `rule` (null = no rule, `default_route`), `model`
(the first target, `provider/model`), `tool` (the tool the call is
forced to; null = none), `responds` / `instructs` (booleans: the rule
answers directly / adds an instruction).

request.description:
Chat-completions body: `messages`, optional `tools` / `metadata`;
`model` picks the profile (`auto-cost`, ...), default balanced.

aliases.description: Route aliases: what a rule's `route` or an overlay's `routes` names.

base_version.description:
Its version (`AceSpecs.base_version` records the one a spec was
saved against).

default_route.description: Where a turn goes when no rule decides, and when no decider answered.

example.description: A minimal overlay to start from.

features.description:
Request facts rules and target `when` can test without the decider.
Rules on features alone, ahead of every rule that asks a question,
decide without a decider call.

levels.description: Named confidence levels a rule can use instead of a probability.

rules.description:
Base rules in evaluation order. An overlay's rules run before them;
`disable` drops them by id.

spec.description: The platform default every overlay extends, as the router runs it.

tiers.description: Tier aliases, lowest first: what a rule's `min` / `max` names.

oneOf.description:
The active version against today's platform default: drift since it
was saved, and whether it still compiles. Absent without an active
version.

linked_app_ids.description: Apps whose `auto` requests route through this ACE.

threshold.description:
P(yes) (or an option's probability) a rule needs, by default; a
decider may calibrate its own.

type.description:
`yes_no` (test P(yes) with a level, `"very_likely"`, or `gte`),
`choice` / `score` (test option probabilities with `prob_gte` /
`prob_sum_gte`).

feature_only.description: Reads request features only (no decider answers).

profiles.description: Profiles it applies to; empty = all.

route.description:
Route alias or `provider/model` it decides; absent for a rule that
only adjusts or acts.

call_id.description: The deciding call's `x-timbal-call-id`: its trace span.

est_usd_delta.description:
Estimated USD change over the window had the rule been enforced
(positive = more expensive); `None` when no decision could be priced.

priced.description: Decisions behind the estimate (models without prices are left out).

changed.description: Where it would have served another route or model, or answered directly.

needs_decider.description:
Decisions it couldn't evaluate: it needs the decider and the active
version decided on features alone.

base_version.description: Platform default version it was checked against when saved.
Platform default version it was checked against when saved.

prose.description: Routing instructions this version was compiled from, if any.

spec.description: As saved: an overlay on the platform default (`"extends": "default"`).

adjusted.description: Decisions whose route a rule's `min` / `max` moved.

by_decider.description:
`key` = decider that answered (`typesafe/jev-1.14.0`, or the OpenAI
Decisions fallback `openai/gpt-6-luna`); null = no decider answer
(decided on features alone, or every decider failed).

by_model.description: Per call: `key` = the model that actually served.

by_version.description: `key` = spec version; null = served by the platform default.

cache.description:
How much of the calls' prompts came from the provider's prompt cache,
per app and served model, largest prompt volume first.

calls.description: Routed calls, the deciding ones and their pinned tool-loop calls.

decider_errors.description: Decisions where at least one decider in the chain failed.

failed_calls.description: Calls that ended in an upstream error or a transport failure.

failovers.description: Calls served by a later candidate after a failure or a policy denial.

fallbacks.description: Served by the platform default although this ACE was asked for.

hedged.description:
Decisions where a slow decider got the next one asked alongside it
(`inference.hedge_ms`).

served_usd.description: What the served calls cost (the billing ledger is the source of truth).

shadow.description:
Shadow rules: how often they matched and how often enforcing them
would have changed the route, with the latest such decisions.

shadow_versions.description:
Shadow versions (`PUT .../shadow`): how often each would have served
the turn differently.

skipped_decider.description: Decided on request features alone, without a decider call.

ttft_p50_ms.description: Time to the served model's first byte, failovers included.

description.description: One-sentence description of what the action allows.

key.description: Action key to grant on a role.

oneOf.description: Resource shape for typed actions, or null when the action is org-wide.

kind.description: Stable wire name for the resource kind (for example `project` or `project_env`).

segments.description: Ordered segment names that make up the resource path template.

next_page_token.description: Token to fetch the next page, or null if this is the last page.

users.description:

than the page window even when more pages exist.

require_passing.description:
Run the ACE's regression cases first and refuse on a failure. Off by
default so a rollback is never blocked.

already_linked.description:
`true` when this channel was already attached, so the call changed
nothing. Linking is idempotent — retries must not create duplicates,
which would notify the same destination twice per transition.

channel_action.description:
How the underlying `NotificationChannels` row was resolved: referenced
by `id`, deduped onto an identical existing row, or inserted.

AlarmDataHealth.description: An enabled alarm and when the series behind it last produced a datapoint.

denominator_metric_name.description: Set only for ratio alarms, so a caller can tell which side went quiet.

last_datapoint_at.description:
When this alarm could last have evaluated a period.

For a ratio alarm this is the *older* of the two series, because
`ratio_datapoints` yields a datapoint only where both sides have one —
reporting the numerator alone would call an alarm healthy while every
period actually resolves to missing.

`null` = no evaluable period within the metric retention horizon, which
for a ratio alarm includes "one of the two series never reported".

stale.description:
The series has been silent long enough that the alarm is almost
certainly watching something that no longer exists.

Silence is counted from the alarm's creation when that is later than
`last_datapoint_at`, so a freshly created alarm is not accused of being
blind before it has had a chance to see anything. Same judgement
`crate::alarms::staleness` notifies on.

AlarmDims.description:
Metric dimension filters. Omitted = aggregate across that dimension.

Not `Copy` since `label` is owned.

label.description:
Span name behind a trace-derived metric. Scopes the alarm to one
tool/step instead of the sum over every span the filter matched.

AlarmGroupBy.description:
The dimension a fan-out alarm keeps one state per value of.

Without it an alarm watches one series: the dims it names, summed over the
ones it leaves out. An org-wide error rate then hides a small app that is
entirely broken behind a large healthy one, and the only way to see each
app was one alarm per app. With it, the same rule is evaluated for every
value of the dimension that has data, each with its own state.

AlarmGroupOut.description: One group of a fan-out alarm.

key.description:
The value of the `group_by` dimension: an app or project id, or a
label.

last_data_at.description: The last evaluation that found data for the group, to within an hour.

name.description: The app's or project's name, when the key is one that still exists.

clear_threshold.description: Set when this alarm uses hysteresis; see [`CreateAlarmReq`].

denominator_metric_name.description: Set when this is a ratio alarm; see [`CreateAlarmReq`].

oneOf.description: Set when the alarm fans out; see [`CreateAlarmReq`].

groups.description:
The groups of a fan-out alarm that have a state, those in alarm
first. A group not listed is at `insufficient_data`: it has not had
enough data to be judged yet, or it stopped reporting and was dropped.
Empty for an alarm that does not fan out.

project_id.description: Project this alarm belongs to; omitted for org-level alarms.

state.description:
For an alarm that fans out, the summary of its groups: `alarm` while
any group is in alarm, else `ok` once one is, else `insufficient_data`.

AlarmStat.description: Aggregation applied to each evaluation period. Percentiles run from p0.1 to p99.9 in tenths; equivalent spellings such as p95.0 are accepted and returned canonically as p95, while a finer value such as p95.05 is rejected rather than rounded. They are exact rather than interpolated from bins, so they are only available on app.run.duration_ms and cannot be used with denominator_metric_name.

group_key.description:
The group that moved, for an alarm that fans out: an app or project
id, or a label.

reason.description: Evaluation evidence: per-period values, threshold, breaching count.

AllowedAction.description:
One action a principal is effectively allowed to perform, with the
role attachments that grant it.

via.description: Role attachments contributing a matching allow grant.

AppType.description:
Workforce component type as returned by the API.

Unknown values map to [`AppType::Unknown`] so list/get keep working when
new types ship. Request bodies use [`AppTypeInput`], which rejects unknowns.

AttachmentReq.description:
A single (role, scope) attachment in the desired state.

`scope` is an optional hierarchical resource path (`projects:42`,
`projects:42:envs:5`). `null` / omitted = unscoped (the role's grants
apply as-written). The same role may appear multiple times with
different scopes — uniqueness is `(role, scope)`.

AuthProviderState.description: State of a single sign-in method on the settings screen.

configured.description:
Whether provider-specific settings (e.g. a bring-your-own OAuth app) have
been supplied. `false` means the method runs on Timbal's defaults.

enabled.description: Whether end users can sign in with this method.

AutoRoute.description: One route of a router and the models it tries.

models.description:
`provider/model` candidates in the order `auto` tries them. One whose
conditions (e.g. prompt length) don't hold moves behind the others.

serves.description:
The first candidate this organization can use (its policies allow it
and its deployment serves it), which is what the route serves unless
that model fails; `null` when there is none.

AutoRouter.description: One router `auto` can use: the platform default or one of the org's ACEs.

ace.description: The ACE's id; `null` for the platform default.

default_route.description: The route used when no rule picks one.

fallback.description:
Why the platform default serves this ACE (`no_active_version`,
`invalid_spec`, `lookup_failed`); `null` otherwise.

slug.description:
Called as `auto:<slug>`. `null` for the platform default (`auto`) and
for ACEs reached only through the apps linked to them.

version.description: Spec version it routes with; `null` when the platform default serves.

oneOf.description: Replace the column value with a SQL literal expression (e.g. `'***'`).
Non-keyed hash. Use `pseudonymize` for stronger guarantees.
HMAC-keyed deterministic pseudonym. Stable across queries that share `key_ref`.
Truncate a string column to `length` characters, optionally pad-suffixed.
Format-preserving redaction of a payment account number.
Email with the local part hidden (`***@example.com`).
Generalize a date or timestamp to the start of the given unit.
Cap a numeric column at a maximum value.
Power-user pattern replacement.

additionalProperties.description:
Per-column transformation applied to query results when this rule matches.

The full vocabulary is reserved at the API boundary so future deployments
can add masks without breaking existing clients. Only `redact`, `hash`,
and `truncate` are accepted by the current release; the others return
`400` until enforcement ships.

cap_credits.description: Max overage credits the user allows (null = unlimited).

Budget.description:
Credit budget on a project (shared pool), a role (each holder's own
spend), one member (`user` override) or every other user (`user_default`),
or a critical project's reserved minimum (`project_reserve`).

A user's personal limit is the first that exists of: their `user`
override, the strictest budget among their roles, `user_default`. Project
budgets apply on top. For per-user budgets, `current_credits` is the
spend of the user it caps (`user`) or of the top spender it governs
(`role`, `user_default`).

A `project_reserve` holds `limit_credits` of the org's monthly cap for its
project: once the cap's headroom is down to what reserves still hold,
other projects move on to grants and overage, or are blocked without
them. `current_credits` is the project's spend this period and
`remaining_credits` the part of the reserve still held.

BudgetPatchBody.description: Partial budget update — merge rows without touching other configured targets.

BudgetPatchInput.description: One budget change in a PATCH merge. `limit_credits: null` removes the budget.

limit_credits.description: When null, removes the budget for this target. When set, must be > 0.

user_id.description: Required for `user` budgets: an active member of the org.

users.description:
Per-member desired attachment sets. Applied atomically: if any entry
is rejected the whole request fails and nothing is written. A member

The org's compute pool draw broken down per project, environment, and

Total pool capacity from purchased machines. `null` = unlimited

The box's own answer over its data tunnel, asked for this response
(through whichever API instance holds the tunnel). Only on the
single-connector view; `null` in lists, when the box holds no tunnel,
did not answer, or is older than 0.1.34.

The connector is too old to connect: it keeps trying and is refused.
It stays offline until someone upgrades it on the box; nothing can be
pushed to it. Goes back to `false` once it is seen connected again.

KB directory files land under (root when omitted). A recursive copy
recreates the tree below it.

max_total_bytes.description: Job cap on aggregate raw bytes. Omit for the node default (2 GiB).

parse.description:
Parse + embed after storing. Default `false` — copy is store-only; the
KB's auto-processing setting never applies to connector copies.

path.description:
Path relative to the root: a file, or a directory when `recursive`.
Empty / omitted / whitespace = the filesystem root (same as the
connector's `CopyFileJob` / browse verbs).

recursive.description:
`true` = `path` is a directory: walk it and stream every regular file
(symlinks skipped). Copying a directory without it is refused node-side.

credits.description: Credits the customer pays (`charged` on the ledger).

waived_credits.description:
Credits forgiven via on-us discounts. Usually 0; when > 0 the chart
overlays it as the muted "On us" series. `credits + waived_credits`
is the write-time pin (gross).

CostsBy.description: How spend inside each costs bin is grouped.

CoverageGap.description:
A feature EU hosting doesn't cover: its data is processed outside the EU
even while EU hosting is on.

slug.description: `auto:<slug>` handle. Omit for an ACE reached only through app links.

cases.description: One or more cases (e.g. the `cases` a compile proposed).

channel.description: Channel: inline `type` + `config`, or reuse with `{ "id": <channel id> }` (same org).

clear_threshold.description:
Hysteresis: once in `alarm`, a period only stops counting as breaching
once it clears *this* value rather than `threshold`. Must sit on the
non-breaching side of `threshold` — below it for `gt`/`gte`, above for
`lt`/`lte`.

Fire at `0.05` and clear at `0.03`, and a metric hovering on 5% produces
one transition instead of one per swing. Without it the only defences
against flapping are a longer `period_seconds` or a higher
`datapoints_to_alarm`, both of which also delay the *first* detection.

datapoints_to_alarm.description: Datapoints that must breach out of the last `evaluation_periods`.

denominator_metric_name.description:
Turns the alarm into a **ratio** condition: each period's datapoint
becomes `metric_name / denominator_metric_name`, read with the same
dims, stat and period. `threshold` is then a rate — `0.05` for a 5%
error rate, not `5`.

Pair it with `min_sample_count`; see that field.

oneOf.description:
Fan the alarm out: evaluate the same rule for every value of this
dimension that has data, each with its own state, instead of once for
their sum. `workforce_id` is one state per app, `project_id` one per
project, `label` one per label.

One message is sent per evaluation, listing the groups that entered
alarm and those that recovered, however many moved. An app that ships
later is covered from its first datapoint. A group that stops
reporting keeps its state for 72 hours and is then dropped, with a
message if it was in alarm.

The dimension must be left out of `dims`. Not available with a
percentile `stat`, nor on the sampled credit and budget levels. A
project alarm (`project_id` set) has to name that project in
`dims.project_id`, since the breakdown shows more than a total does.

metric_name.description:
Metric to watch, e.g. `app.run.errors`, `deployment.health`,
`org.credits.spend`. The numerator when `denominator_metric_name` is set.

min_sample_count.description:
Minimum denominator for a ratio period to count. Below it (or at zero)
the period has no datapoint and follows `missing_data`.

Exists because ratios are meaningless on tiny samples: 1 error out of 1
run is 100%. Set it to the smallest traffic level you'd actually act on.

oneOf.description:
Omit to get a policy chosen from the metric: `ignore` for `trace.*`
(sparse — a gap is absence of data, not a recovery) and `not_breaching`
for everything else. An alarm with `group_by` gets `ignore` whatever
its metric: one app's series has gaps even when the org's doesn't.

period_seconds.description: Length of one evaluation period in seconds (multiple of 60, >= 60).

project_id.description: Scope the alarm to a project. Omit for an org-level alarm.

dry_run.description: When omitted or when the request has no JSON body, treated as `false`.

force.description:
Create the backup even if the knowledge base is currently served by
another host. Defaults to `false`, in which case such requests are
rejected with `409 Conflict`.

Channel reference embedded in another resource's create body (alarms).

OAuth client secret. Encrypted at rest; never returned on read.
Required for `oidc`.

Optional catch-all role for JIT members whose group claim matched no
mapping. When omitted, such members are added with no role (a bare
member, pending an admin grant) rather than an implicit default.
Accepts a number or a stringified id (`2227` or `"2227"`).

groups_claim.description: Claim carrying group membership. Defaults to `groups`.

IdP issuer / discovery base; `/.well-known/openid-configuration` is
fetched from here. **Required for `oidc`; ignored for `directory`.**

Connection kind. Defaults to `oidc` (backward-compatible). Use
`directory` for a login-less SCIM connection: no issuer/client creds
required, it only anchors SCIM group→role mappings + the catch-all role.

provider_key.description:
Stable, URL-safe handle used in the login URL
(`/auth/sso/{provider_key}`) and the signed OAuth state. Lowercase
letters/digits/hyphens; must not collide with the built-in social
providers. Globally unique.

row_filter_dsl.description:
Row predicate: `{"const": bool}` or `{"sql": "<expr>"}`. The `sql`
form admits columns of `table_name`, literals, comparisons,
`AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] IN (…)`, `BETWEEN`,
`[I]LIKE` and `user_id()` (the caller's user id). Anything else —
other tables, functions, subqueries — is a 400 naming the construct.

CreateMetricDefinitionReq.description:
Body for **POST** `/orgs/{org_id}/metrics/definitions`.

Every predicate field is optional and they AND together. All omitted means
"every non-root span", which paired with `label_source: span_name` gives a
per-step call count — a reasonable first definition.

Exact span name — the leaf of the span path (`llm`, `get_address`),
not the full `{workforce}.{step}`.

oneOf.description: Rule effect. Defaults to `deny`.

model_id.description: Model to target. Omit to target every model of the provider.

livemode.description: Stripe live mode for billing. Superadmin-only; ignored for other callers.

Business context the agent has before its first turn: a JSON object
of up to 64 fields (16 KiB), values kept as JSON. `call_id`,
`direction`, `from`, `to`, `user_number` and `agent_number` are set by
the platform and reserved.

Per-call opener, spoken verbatim the moment the callee picks up;
beats whatever the agent declared. Omitted → the agent's own
`voice_config` decides: `outbound_greeting` if set (`""` there means
stay quiet and wait for the callee's "hello"), else `greeting`.
`""` here is the same as omitting it.

oneOf.description: The workflow run that placed the call, for traceability.

trunk_id.description:
SIP trunk to dial through. Omitted → the organization's only ready
outbound trunk (the only one presenting `from_number`, when given).

grants.description:
Grants this role carries. Empty list is allowed (creates a no-op
role; admin can extend it later).

Role name. Must be unique within the org. Reserved system names
(`admin`, `developer`, `billing`, `member`, `user`) are rejected.

The run's input, for apps that take more than a prompt. Defaults to
`{"prompt": instruction}`.

The thread fires continue: the id of its first run, which must be the
caller's own. Omitted, every fire starts a new thread.

Create response: the only time the plaintext token is ever returned. The
caller (IdP admin) must copy `token` now — it can't be retrieved later.

dest_table.description:
Destination table inside the KB. Created by the first run when it
doesn't exist yet; when it does, `existing_dest` decides whether the
sync continues it or rebuilds it.

oneOf.description:
How to treat a `dest_table` that already exists. Defaults to `adopt`.
Only meaningful for an incremental sync — a full-refresh one replaces the
destination on every run by definition.

initial_cursor.description:
Checkpoint to continue an existing `dest_table` from, overriding the one
read off the table itself. Only valid when the table exists and
`existing_dest` is `adopt` — for a table the sync still has to build,
use `start_cursor`. Same shape as `start_cursor`.

interval_secs.description:
Seconds between run *starts*. The scheduler ticks every 30s, so smaller
values effectively mean "every tick".

kb_id.description: Target KB (numeric id, same as the `/k2` routes).

key_columns.description:
Ordered destination `PRIMARY KEY` columns. Omit for a keyless table. The
first run declares the key; later runs then **merge** on it (upsert) so an
upstream update — or a re-pulled boundary row from a non-unique cursor —
overwrites in place instead of duplicating. Key columns are auto-added to
a `columns` subset, so they only need to exist on the source table. Source
these from the browse columns' `pk_position`.

start_cursor.description:
Optional lower bound for the **first** run when it builds the table:
only rows with `cursor_column >= start_cursor` are pulled (e.g. seed a
timestamp to backfill "from last month on" instead of the whole table).
Ignored on later runs — the advancing cursor takes over — and ignored
when the sync adopts an existing table. Shape matches the job `cursor`
(e.g. `{"kind":"timestamp","value":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"}`). Not valid
on a full-refresh sync (no `cursor_column` to bound).

adopted_dest_table.description:
`true` when the sync continues an existing destination table instead of
building it on the first run.

initial_cursor.description:
The checkpoint the first run resumes from when the destination was
adopted; `null` otherwise (including an adopted table that was empty).

key_columns.description:
Primary-key columns the sync will merge on. Inherited from an adopted
table's own key when the request didn't declare one.

name.description: Optional display name for the new component. If omitted, a unique name is generated.

Credits awarded by this grant. Always positive; corrections ship as a
separate grant rather than a negative amount.

Credits already drawn from this grant by attributed costs. Bounded by
`amount_credits`; remaining headroom is `amount_credits - consumed_credits`.

Set once the grant has been fully consumed by usage; `null` while

When `true`, delete even if alarms reference this channel (cascading
unlink). Still refused when it would leave an enabled alarm with no
channels.

Public-API representation of a single deployment row, returned by the
env-scoped deployments list endpoint. Flattens the runtime config
(cpu/memory/...) inline rather than nesting under `config` — frontend
consumes the fields directly.

DeploymentTarget.description:
Image/version pointer embedded in [`DeploymentDetail::target`]. Distinct
from [`crate::deployments::models::DeployTarget`] (the domain-layer spec
carrying image URIs / platform). This shape is the public-API view of
what a deployment is *of*.

batch_rows.description: Target rows per batch. Defaults to 5000.

cursor.description: Resume checkpoint; omit for a full initial extract.

kb_id.description: Target KB (numeric id, same as the `/k2` routes).

key_columns.description:
Ordered destination `PRIMARY KEY` columns. Omit for a keyless table.
Honored when the run builds the table (`create`/`replace`). Key columns
are auto-added to a `source.columns` subset, so they only need to exist
on the source table. Source these from the browse columns' `pk_position`
for a faithful copy of the source key.

mode.description:
`create` | `append` | `replace` | `upsert`. Defaults to `create`.
`upsert` merges each batch on `key_columns` (rows with an existing key are
overwritten, new keys inserted); requires non-empty `key_columns`. If the
destination table doesn't exist yet, the first upsert builds it keyed.

oneOf.description:
Optional load-shaping for gentle extraction against busy source systems.
Omit for no throttle.

placement.description:
Where the KB's data lives: `hosted` (control-plane KB, the default) or
`local` (a KB runtime inside the connector's environment — requires the
connector to advertise the `kb:local` capability).

project_env.description: Project environment this domain is linked to, if any

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp in epoch milliseconds

validation_records.description: DNS records required for SSL certificate validation

Name for the new project. Defaults to the source name with a " copy"
suffix, de-duplicated within the organization.
